messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: prod-eu-gpu cluster queue > 85% for 7m, 95th latency spike, autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. Pager: high-priority.

eric-oncall: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs + checking autoscaler events.

sara-eng: @eric-oncall saw related alerts earlier about launch template drift in another cluster — might be the same class of issue.

mike-infra: looking. quick check: ASG max is at 60, desired 60, queue keeps growing. autoscaler says "scaleUp failed" with attach/iam errors.

jordan-sre: paste autoscaler error logs?

eric-oncall: here's the autoscaler-controller logs (tail):
```
E0307 09:16:21.123 autoscaler.go:412] scaleUp: failed to create nodes for nodegroup "gpu-prod-ng": error creating launch configuration: LaunchTemplateNameMismatch: LaunchTemplate "lt-gpu-v3" not found for account, expected "lt-gpu-v2"
Caused by: ec2:AttachRolePolicy: AccessDenied: arn:aws:iam::123456:role/RedwoodNodeRole not allowed to passrole
```

mike-infra: that passrole AccessDenied means the node role's policy changed or a temporary credentials issue when creating instances. Could be token expiry on the worker that provisions launchtemplate versions.

lex-support: customer-impact: embedding API percent queued rising from 2% -> 28%, median latency for queued requests now 9s -> 40s. Several customers reported timeouts. cc @sara-eng for product impact.

sara-eng: thanks. We're seeing backpressure: prefix cache miss + burst from batch jobs. Can we open manual capacity?

mike-infra: attempting manual scale: updating ASG and creating new nodegroup as temp fallback. starting with updating ASG max to 80.

eric-oncall: runbook step: try nodegroup create with explicit launch template version that exists. tagging for quick deletion after.

mike-infra: running command:
```bash
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name asg-prod-gpu --max-size 80 --desired-capacity 70
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster prod-eu --name ng-temp-gpu --node-type p4d.24xlarge --nodes 6 --node-ami auto --node-role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/RedwoodNodeRole --launch-template "LaunchTemplateId=lt-0abcd1234,Version=3"
```

mike-infra: create nodegroup failing: API returns "AccessDenied: Cannot pass role RedwoodNodeRole to EC2". same passrole issue.

jordan-sre: can you paste iam simulate or policy output?

mike-infra: fetched instance profile and role; looks intact. However STS calls log shows InvalidIdentityToken on the provisioning service for a 5m window starting 09:12 UTC. Might be short-lived token expiration for the control-plane agent that signs launchtemplate requests.

eric-oncall: if control-plane agent's token expired, services trying to create instances will get AttachRole/PassRole denied. Short term: spin up warm nodes from existing image (no new LT creation) by increasing desired capacity on ASG that's already configured.

mike-infra: I can increase desired on the ASG that has the correct LT & role:
```bash
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name asg-prod-gpu-warm --desired-capacity 30 --honor-cooldown false
```

mike-infra: done. launching 6 warm nodes from existing ASG, will show in kubernetes as NotReady then Ready after bootstrap.

lex-support: will message impacted customers: high queuing, mitigation in progress, ETA ~10-15m for warm nodes to reach Ready.

sara-eng: applying temporary throttling & rate-limit mitigation: reducing batch size for non-critical jobs, increasing concurrency backpressure to keep inference tails sane. Patch rolled to routing layer.

jordan-sre: autoscaler still logging launch template mismatch errors for the primary nodegroup. suspect orchestration attempted to roll LT to v4 earlier today and partial state left. need infra to reconcile launchtemplate id/version on the nodegroup.

mike-infra: I'm checking CloudTrail: at 09:10 there was a failed LT create due to quota; then at 09:11 an automated job retried with wrong parameters and created lt-0abcd1234 (v3) while kube nodegroup still expects lt-0abcd9876 (v2). That explains mismatch.

eric-oncall: manual reconciliation options: 1) update nodegroup to point to the new LT id (safer if we confirm AMI/kernel parity), 2) rollback/retire the new LT and re-create expected LT id (harder), 3) keep warm nodes from the warm ASG and cordon/pod-evict workloads to them.

mike-infra: plan: 1) keep warm nodes up to relieve queue. 2) schedule nodegroup update to use lt-0abcd1234.v3 after quick compatibility smoke check on a single node. 3) revert the automations that created the mismatched LT.

sara-eng: ack. prepping smoke test harness for model restore. will run inference test (small sample) as soon as node appears.

lex-support: status update to customers sent. slack thread pinned to incident channel.

deploy-bot: NOTE: rolling job pipeline detected a launchtemplate update at 08:59 by pipeline:infra/cicd (run #482).

mike-infra: correlating that pipeline run with new LT id creation. CICD used template name param "lt-gpu-v3" which wasn't propagated to kube config. pipeline owner pinged.

jordan-sre: smoke test looks good on node ng-temp-1 (single test):
```
Request: embed("openai") -> latency 120ms, token cost normal, no OOM, gpu mem 85%
```

eric-oncall: proceeding to update nodegroup pointer to LT v3 for the primary gpu nodegroup. will do in canary: cordon one zone then update.

mike-infra: command:
```bash
eksctl utils update-nodegroup-configuration --cluster prod-eu --name gpu-prod-ng --launch-template-id lt-0abcd1234 --launch-template-version 3
```

mike-infra: update applied in zone-a canary. new nodes launching and joining.

sara-eng: traffic shifted to new nodes, queue dropped from 28% -> 7% after 2 mins. latency recovering.

lex-support: sending customer follow-up: recovery in progress, some requests may have timed out earlier, recommend retry.

jordan-sre: follow-up: root cause: automated pipeline rolled a launch template name/version that was not reconciled with the cluster's nodegroup config. When the autoscaler attempted dynamic creation it hit a PassRole/AttachPolicy denial likely due to a transient STS token expiration for the provisioning service which compounded the failure.

eric-oncall: lessons: 1) prevent pipelines from creating LTs without updating cluster configs atomically. 2) add autoscaler fallback to warm-asg route earlier. 3) alert on mismatched LT ids between ASG/nodegroup and cluster config.

mike-infra: created ticket INFRA-4123 to revert pipeline parameterization, add a preflight check in cicd that validates nodegroup LT id/version in eks config store.

sara-eng: created follow-up task PROD-queue-eval for evaluating caching/batching to reduce peak bursts.

lex-support: customers notified in status page; incident will be updated with timeline & postmortem.

eric-oncall: handing off to mike-infra for post-incident cleanup and root cause write-up. thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike-infra: taking postmortem, will update INFRA-4123 and notify security if there are IAM policy concerns.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: prod-eu-gpu queue mitigated at 09:40 UTC, autoscaler failures remediated, ticket INFRA-4123 created.
